name: Punta Cana
title: Holidays in Punta Cana
intro: Long white beaches fringed with coconut palms on the Dominican Republic's eastern tip, with all-inclusive resorts and warm, clear sea. Here's what Punta Cana is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: Palm trees leaning over a white-sand beach in Punta Cana

facts.label: Time difference
facts.value: 4 hrs behind the UK (5 in winter)

facts_note: Fill in the free e-Ticket form online before you fly in and out. Hurricane season runs from June to November, peaking from August to October. Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: December to April is the best time: dry, sunny and less humid, but also the priciest. May to November is hotter and more humid, with short showers, and hurricane season peaks from August to October. Summer is still busy and good value.

things.name: Bávaro Beach
things.blurb: Kilometres of white sand and calm water, with resorts all along it.

things.name: Saona Island
things.blurb: Catamaran trips to a national-park island with starfish shallows.

things.name: Hoyo Azul
things.blurb: A turquoise freshwater pool at the foot of a cliff in Scape Park.

things.name: Snorkelling and diving
things.blurb: Reef trips along the coast, with turtles and tropical fish.

things.name: Altos de Chavón
things.blurb: A replica 16th-century Mediterranean village above a river gorge.

things.name: Macao Beach
things.blurb: A wilder public beach with surfing and local fish shacks.

faqs.question: Is Punta Cana only all-inclusive?
faqs.answer: Mostly, yes. Resorts dominate, though there are some apartments and smaller hotels.

faqs.question: Do you need a visa for the Dominican Republic?
faqs.answer: UK passport holders don't need one for a holiday, but must complete the free online e-Ticket before arrival and departure.

faqs.question: Is there seaweed in Punta Cana?
faqs.answer: Sargassum seaweed can wash up from spring to autumn. Resorts clear it, and the beaches further north are often less affected.
